He used to sing in a barbershop quartet, you know. They performed at the town gazebo last Fourth of July. The weather was just frightfully hot that day, nearly ninety degrees, and they were all wearing those heavy striped blazers and straw boater hats. I felt so bad for them, standing out there in the blazing sun. I had brought my favorite parasol—the one with the delicate lace trim I found at an antique shop in Vermont—but even that wasn't enough to keep the heat off. We ended up having to leave early and get ice cream at that little parlor on Elm Street, the one that makes their own waffle cones. The smell of the vanilla batter cooking on those cast-iron presses is just heavenly, though the line is always out the door...\n\nOh, goodness gracious. I've always wanted to visit New Mexico, the sunsets are supposed to be just spectacular out there, all those burnt oranges and deep purples. My aunt used to paint watercolors of desert landscapes, though she lived in Ohio her entire life. She had this little studio out on her sunporch, but the draft in the winter was just unbearable. They had to tape plastic wrap over the glass to keep the cold out, and it always made this awful crinkling sound whenever the wind blew... \n\nOh, dear me. I've done it again, haven't I? I am so sorry, Doctor, my mind just completely takes off without me sometimes. But yes, about work... I am still there, but I've really had to lean on my colleagues to help me get through our planning meetings. And outside of school, I've just stopped being reliable entirely. The book club, the theater planning, the neighborhood events... I just haven't been able to manage them."
